In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in general, the spectrum of the graph Laplacian does not converge to the spectrum of the limit operator, even if the graph is constructed from a well-behaves kernel function.

, for a given kernel, there is an infinite set of possible graph constructions that converge to a limit operator, and for each of these, the limit operator is well-defined and has a convergent spectrum.
, for a given graph construction with shrinking neighborhoods, the limit operator can be characterized in terms of the limit of the graph Laplacian.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a framework to analyze the asymptotic properties of graph Laplacian matrices.
the limit operator is a linear operator that maps a function on the graph vertices to the same space, and that the convergence is in terms of the graph topology.
the limit operator of graph Laplacian depends on the kernel and the graph construction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the convergence of graph Laplacian spectra can be achieved without requiring smoothness of the kernel function.
, for many graph constructions, the limit operator is the same as the limit operator of the graph Laplacian.
the choice of graph construction is a crucial factor in analyzing the asymptotic properties of graph Laplacian operators.
